raw_response:
I will do it much like last year, with a few small adjustments based on cost and what I saw in nearby fields. I farm 20 mu, so I cannot be careless, but I also cannot save too hard on fertilizer and lose yield. We have well irrigation, and that helps a lot for both wheat and maize. Around here in Quzhou County, if wheat is short of fertilizer or misses water at the key time, the heads are small and the grain is light. Maize is the same: if I save too much on nitrogen, the stalk looks fine at first but the ear is not full. I finished primary school, so I do pay attention to seed, fertilizer, and timing, but I still mainly do what has proved reliable in our area. For wheat I will keep improved seed, put more fertilizer at the start, then add nitrogen later at jointing with water. For maize I will use hybrid seed, because the local hybrids usually yield better and stand better if the summer rain and wind come hard. Since some family members work off-farm, I will keep the work simple and efficient, so I will mostly use rotary tillage and not make the field work too complicated. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer and one proper pesticide spray than gamble with the harvest. With water from the well and normal weather, I will aim for decent wheat and maize yields, not the highest possible, but steady and safe.
